correctness.rationale: A finite-index invariant quadric for a connected semisimple projective group would yield an invariant symmetric tensor. The standard symplectic representation has no such tensor, while PSp(2m,R) is a proper algebraic subgroup of PSL(2m,R), so it is non-elementary under the quadric definition but not ambient-Zariski-dense.

originality.rationale: The representation-theoretic ingredients are classical and are not claimed as new. Searches found no prior answer applying the standard projective symplectic subgroup to Faraco--Rungi's newly posed Problem 1.6 or identifying projective dimension three as the first failure.

value.rationale: The result gives a sharp negative answer to the proposed higher-dimensional equivalence, supplies an infinite counterexample family and discrete surface-group examples, and isolates the structural reason quadrics cease to detect all proper algebraic subgroups.
